## Proof

We compute $|\mathrm{SL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})|$ via the reduction map and the determinant map.

**Step 1: $|\mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})|$.**

Consider the reduction homomorphism
$$\pi: \mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z}) \to \mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbb{F}_p), \quad A \bmod p^k \mapsto A \bmod p.$$
It is surjective: any lift of an invertible mod-$p$ matrix to $\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z}$ remains invertible (its determinant is a unit mod $p$, hence a unit mod $p^k$).

Its kernel is $\{I + pB : B \in M_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^{k-1}\mathbb{Z})\}$. Indeed $I+pB$ is always invertible (inverse given by the finite geometric series $(I+pB)^{-1} = I - pB + p^2 B^2 - \cdots$), and $\det(I+pB)\equiv 1\pmod p$. The map $B \mapsto I+pB$ is a bijection $M_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^{k-1}\mathbb{Z}) \to \ker\pi$, so
$$|\ker\pi| = |M_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^{k-1}\mathbb{Z})| = p^{36(k-1)}.$$

The order of $\mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbb{F}_p)$ is
$$|\mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbb{F}_p)| = \prod_{i=0}^{5}(p^6 - p^i) = p^{0+1+2+3+4+5}\prod_{j=1}^{6}(p^j-1) = p^{15}\prod_{j=1}^{6}(p^j-1).$$

Therefore
$$|\mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})| = p^{15}\prod_{j=1}^{6}(p^j-1)\cdot p^{36(k-1)}.$$

**Step 2: Divide by $|(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})^\times|$ to get $|\mathrm{SL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})|$.**

The determinant map
$$\det: \mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z}) \to (\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})^\times$$
is surjective: for any unit $u$, the diagonal matrix $\mathrm{diag}(u,1,1,1,1,1)$ lies in $\mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})$ and has determinant $u$. Its kernel is by definition $\mathrm{SL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})$, so
$$|\mathrm{SL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})| = \frac{|\mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})|}{|(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})^\times|}.$$

Since $|(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})^\times| = \varphi(p^k) = p^{k-1}(p-1)$, and the factor $(p^1-1)=(p-1)$ appears in $\prod_{j=1}^{6}(p^j-1)$, we obtain

$$|\mathrm{SL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})| = \frac{p^{15}\,\prod_{j=1}^{6}(p^j-1)\cdot p^{36(k-1)}}{p^{k-1}(p-1)} = p^{15}\,\prod_{j=2}^{6}(p^j-1)\cdot p^{36(k-1)-(k-1)}.$$

Since $36(k-1)-(k-1)=35(k-1)$ and $15+35(k-1)=35k-20$,

$$\boxed{|\mathrm{SL}_6(\mathbb{Z}/p^k\mathbb{Z})| = p^{35k-20}\,(p^2-1)(p^3-1)(p^4-1)(p^5-1)(p^6-1).}$$

**Sanity check ($k=1$):** the formula gives $p^{15}\prod_{j=2}^{6}(p^j-1)$, which equals $|\mathrm{GL}_6(\mathbb{F}_p)|/(p-1)=|\mathrm{SL}_6(\mathbb{F}_p)|$, the standard value. ✓
